Claim age and claim\n62\t/// recency are independent of worker liveness so a worker name that is reused\n63\t/// by a relaunch cannot pin an abandoned bead forever.\n64\tasync fn cleanup_in_progress(\n65\t    store: &dyn BeadStore,\n66\t    registry: &Registry,\n67\t    telemetry: &Telemetry,\n68\t    qualified_id: &str,\n69\t    claim_ttl: Option<Duration>,\n70\t) -> Result<u32> {\n71\t    let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;\n72\t\n73\t    // Registry::list() does blocking file I/O and PID checks.\n74\t    // Use spawn_blocking to avoid blocking the async executor.\n75\t    let registry_for_blocking = registry.clone();\n76\t    let workers = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || registry_for_blocking.list())\n77\t        .await\n78\t        .context(\"spawn_blocking task for registry.list() failed\")?\n79\t        .context(\"registry.list() failed\")?;\n80\t\n81\t    // Build a set of fully-qualified worker IDs for registered, alive workers.\n82\t    let live_worker_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = workers\n83\t        .iter()\n84\t        .filter(|w| HealthMonitor::check_pid_alive(w.pid))\n85\t        .map(|w| w.id.clone())\n86\t        .collect();\n87\t\n88\t    // For each assignee with multiple in_progress beads, identify which bead\n89\t    // has the MAX updated_at (the only plausible active claim). This catches claims leaked by the\n130\t        // dispatch layer even when the worker's session/process is still\n131\t        // alive, including when this is the current worker's own identity.\n132\t        let newest_claim = newest_bead_by_assignee.get(assignee);\n133\t        let is_superseded = newest_claim\n134\t            .map(|(newest_updated, _)| bead.updated_at < *newest_updated)\n135\t            .unwrap_or(false);\n136\t        if is_superseded {\n137\t            if let Some((_, newest_bead_id)) = newest_claim {\n138\t                tracing::info!(\n139\t                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n140\t                    assignee = %assignee,\n141\t                    age_secs = claim_age.map_or(0, |age| age.as_secs()),\n142\t                    newest_bead_id = %newest_bead_id,\n143\t                    \"releasing in-progress bead superseded by newer claim from same assignee\"\n144\t                );\n145\t            }\n146\t        }\n147\t\n148\t        // Claim age is an independent release condition. A live worker may\n149\t        // still hold an abandoned claim, especially when --count 1 relaunches\n150\t        // under the same worker name indefinitely.\n151\t        if !is_superseded && !stale_by_age && assignee == qualified_id {\n152\t            continue;\n153\t        }\n154\t\n155\t        // Skip if the assignee matches a registered, alive worker unless the\n156\t        // claim has exceeded its age limit. Workers register with fully-qualified\n157\t        // IDs ({adapter}-{worker_id}), so this comparison prevents collisions\n158\t        // when workers from different adapter pools share a NATO name.\n159\t        if !is_superseded && !stale_by_age && live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) {\n160\t            continue;\n161\t        }\n162\t\n163\t        let reason = match (is_superseded, newest_claim) {\n164\t            (true, Some((_, newest_bead_id))) => {\n165\t                format!(\"superseded by newer in-progress claim {newest_bead_id} from same assignee\")\n166\t            }\n167\t            (false, _) if stale_by_age => {\n168\t                let age_secs = claim_age.map_or(0, |age| age.as_secs());\n169\t                format!(\"stale claim: age {age_secs}s exceeds configured claim TTL\")\n170\t            }\n171\t            _ => format!(\"orphaned: assignee {assignee} has no live worker\"),\n172\t        };\n173\t\n174\t        tracing::info!(\n175\t            bead_id = %bead.id,\n176\t            assignee = %assignee,\n177\t            age_secs = claim_age.map_or(0, |age| age.as_secs()),\n178\t {\n184\t            Ok(()) => {\n185\t                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n186\t                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n187\t                    reason,\n188\t                });\n189\t                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::StuckReleased {\n190\t                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n191\t                    peer_worker: assignee.clone(),\n192\t                });\n193\t                released += 1;\n194\t            }\n195\t            Err(e) => {\n196\t                tracing::warn!(\n197\t cycle.\n214\t#[derive(Debug, Default)]\n215\tstruct MendSummary {\n216\t    beads_released: u32,\n217\t    locks_removed: u32,\n218\t    deps_cleaned: u32,\n219\t    db_repaired: bool,\n220\t changes bead store state.\n238\t    ///\n239\t    /// Only operations that add or release claimable beads should return true.\n240\t    /// A strand MUST return `WorkCreated` only when it inserts a claimable bead\n241\t    /// into the store that the waterfall will re-scan. No-op cleanup (pruning\n242\t    /// traces, removing stale locks, repairing DB) should return `NoWork`.\n243\t    ///\n244\t    /// Operations that return `WorkCreated`:\n245\t    /// - `beads_released > 0`: Orphaned beads were released back to Open status.\n246\t    /// - `deps_cleaned > 0`: Stale dependency links were removed (beads become claimable).\n247\t    /// - `assignees_cleared > 0`: Stale assignees were cleared (beads become claimable).\n248\t    ///\n249\t    /// Operations that return `NoWork` (maintenance, not work creation):\n250\t    /// - event identifying\n256\t    /// the created bead(s) so operators can see what the restart is chasing.\n257\t    fn did_work(&self) -> bool {\n258\t        // Bead release, dependency removal, and assignee clearing add claimable items to the queue.\n259\t        // Lock removal, DB repair, and DB rebuild are maintenance operations\n260\t        // that don't create new work and must not trigger a waterfall restart.\n261\t        self.beads_released > 0 || self.deps_cleaned > 0 || self.assignees_cleared > 0\n262\t    }\n263\t}\n264\t\n265\t/// The Mend strand — maintenance and  /// Remove claim lock files that are not actively held by any process.\n    ///\n    /// This function immediately cleans up lock files whose holding process\n    /// has died, without waiting for an age-based timeout. The flock(2) lock\n    /// is automatically released by the kernel when the holder process dies,\n    /// so try_acquire_flock() will succeed immediately and we can remove the\n    /// stale metadata file.\n    ///\n    /// Lock files older than lock_ttl_secs are also cleaned up as a fallback\n    /// to handle edge cases where the flock probe might fail.\n    fn cleanup_orphaned_locks(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        let lock_ttl = Duration::from_secs(self.config.lock_ttl_secs);\n\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&self.lock_dir) {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    dir = %self.lock_dir.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to read lock directory\"\n                );\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = match entry {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let path = entry.path();\n            let name = match path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) {\n                Some(n) => n,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Only consider needle claim lock files.\n            if !name.starts_with(\"needle-claim-\") || !name.ends_with(\".lock\") {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check file age for logging/fallback cleanup.\n            let age = match file_age(&path) {\n                Some(age) => age,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Try to acquire flock (non-blocking). If we can acquire it,\n            // no one is holding it — safe to delete immediately.\n            //\n            // The kernel releases flocks when the holder process dies, so this\n            // probe succeeds immediately for dead PIDs regardless of file age.\n            match try_acquire_flock(&path) {\n                Ok(Some(_file)) => {\n                    // Lock acquired — no one holds it. Remove the file.\n                    let age_secs = age.as_secs();\n                    if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_file(&path) {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove orphaned lock file\"\n                        );\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendLockRemoveFailed {\n                            lock_path: path.display().to_string(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                        });\n                        continue;\n                    }\n\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        age_secs,\n                        \"removed orphaned lock file\"\n                    );\n\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendOrphanedLockRemoved {\n                        lock_path: path.display().to_string(),\n                        age_secs,\n                    });\n\n                    summary.locks_removed += 1;\n                }\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    // Lock is actively held — skip.\n                    // Only log if the file is old; otherwise it's just a normal active lock.\n                    if age > lock_ttl {\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            age_secs = age.as_secs(),\n                            \"lock file is old but actively held, skipping\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::debug!(\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to probe lock file\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 3: Dependency link repair ───────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Find open beads that have closed blockers and clean up the stale\n    /// dependency links.\n    ///\n    /// br does not automatically resolve dependency links on bead closure,\n    /// so a bead can remain blocked even after its blocker is closed.\n    async fn cleanup_stale_dependencies(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        summary: &mut MendSummary,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let all_beads = store.list_all().await?;\n\n        for bead in &all_beads {\n            // Only check open beads that have dependencies.\n            if bead.status != BeadStatus::Open || bead.dependencies.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            for dep in &bead.dependencies {\n                // Only check \"blocks\" type dependencies where the blocker is closed.\n                if dep.dependency_type != \"blocks\" {\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                if dep.status == \"closed\" {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        blocker_id = %dep.id,\n                        \"removing stale dependency link (closed blocker on open bead)\"\n                    );\n\n                    // Remove the stale dependency link.\n                    match store.remove_dependency(&bead.id, &dep.id).await {\n                        Ok(()) => {\n                            // Emit telemetry for the removed dependency.\n                            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendDependencyRemoved {\n                                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                                blocker_id: dep.id.clone(),\n                            });\n                            summary.deps_cleaned += 1;\n                        }\n                        Err(e) => {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                blocker_id = %dep.id,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to remove stale dependency link\"\n                            );\n                            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendDependencyCleanupFailed {\n                                bead_id: bead.id.to_string(),\n                                blocker_id: dep.id.to_string(),\n                                error: e.to_string(),\n                            });\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 3.5: Dead worker registry cleanup ───────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Scan the worker registry and remove entries for dead PIDs.\n    ///\n    /// This proactive cleanup ensures that dead worker entries don't accumulate\n    /// in the registry. The registry's list() method already filters dead PIDs,\n    /// but that only happens when rate limit checks run. This step ensures\n    /// cleanup happens every mend cycle.\n    fn cleanup_dead_workers(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read the raw registry file to find entries that need cleanup.\n        let raw_content = match std::fs::read_to_string(self.registry.path()) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to read registry file\");\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        let raw_reg: crate::registry::RegistryFile = match serde_json::from_str(&raw_content) {\n            Ok(r) => r,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to parse registry file\");\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        for entry in &raw_reg.workers {\n            // Skip our own entry.\n            if entry.id == self.qualified_id {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check if the PID is dead.\n            if crate::registry::is_pid_alive(entry.pid) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dead worker found — deregister it.\n            match self.registry.deregister(&entry.id) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        worker_id = %entry.id,\n                        pid = entry.pid,\n                        \"removed dead worker from registry\"\n                    );\n\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendWorkerDeregistered {\n                        worker_id: entry.id.clone(),\n                        pid: entry.pid,\n                    });\n\n                    summary.workers_deregistered += 1;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %entry.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to deregister dead worker\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 4: Agent log file cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Delete `.agent.jsonl` files in `log_dir` that are older than\n    /// `retention_days` and do not belong to a currently-executing bead.\n    ///\n    /// Also deletes logs from workers that processed 0 beads immediately,\n    /// regardless of age. This cleans up logs from workers that crashed\n    /// before processing any beads.\n    ///\n    /// Files are matched by the `.agent.jsonl` suffix. The bead ID is parsed\n    /// from the stem (`<worker>-<bead>`): a file is considered active if the\n    /// stem ends with `-<bead_id}` for any in-progress bead.\n    async fn cleanup_old_agent_logs(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        summary: &mut MendSummary,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.retention_days == 0 {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&self.log_dir) {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    dir = %self.log_dir.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"mend: failed to read log directory for agent log cleanup\"\n                );\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Collect all .agent.jsonl paths first so we can bail early if none.\n        let agent_log_paths: Vec<PathBuf> = entries\n            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())\n            .map(|e| e.path())\n            .filter(|p| {\n                p.file_name()\n                    .and_then(|n| n.to_str())\n                    .map(|n| n.ends_with(\".agent.jsonl\"))\n                    .unwrap_or(false)\n            })\n            .collect();\n\n        if agent_log_paths.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let cutoff = Duration::from_secs(u64::from(self.retention_days) * 86400);\n\n        // Build the set of currently in-progress bead IDs.\n        let in_progress_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = store\n            .list_all()\n            .await?\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|b| b.status == BeadStatus::InProgress)\n            .map(|b| b.id.as_ref().to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        // Get the registry workers for zero-activity detection.\n        let registry_workers = self.registry.list()?;\n\n        for path in &agent_log_paths {\n            // Skip if this log belongs to an in-progress bead.\n            let stem = match path\n                .file_name()\n                .and_then(|n| n.to_str())\n                .and_then(|n| n.strip_suffix(\".agent.jsonl\"))\n            {\n                Some(s) => s.to_string(),\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            let is_active = in_progress_ids\n                .iter()\n                .any(|bead_id| stem == *bead_id || stem.ends_with(&format!(\"-{bead_id}\")));\n\n            if is_active {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    \"skipping agent log for in-progress bead\"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Extract worker ID from stem. Format is \"{worker_id}-{bead_id}\".\n            // Worker IDs may contain dashes, so we try to find a match in the registry\n            // by checking if any registered worker_id is a prefix of the stem.\n            let worker_id = registry_workers\n                .iter()\n                .find(|w| {\n                    // Stem format: \"{worker_id}-{bead_id}\"\n                    // If worker_id is a prefix of stem followed by a dash, it's a match.\n                    stem.starts_with(&format!(\"{}-\", w.id))\n                })\n                .map(|w| w.id.clone());\n\n            // Check if this is a zero-activity worker log.\n            let is_zero_activity = match worker_id {\n                Some(ref id) => {\n                    // Found in registry — check beads_processed count.\n                    registry_workers\n                        .iter()\n                        .find(|w| &w.id == id)\n                        .map(|w| w.beads_processed == 0)\n                        .unwrap_or(true)\n                }\n                None => {\n                    // Worker not in registry — treat as zero-activity (crashed before registering).\n                    true\n                }\n            };\n\n            if is_zero_activity {\n                // Delete immediately regardless of age.\n                if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"mend: failed to remove zero-activity agent log\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                tracing::info!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    worker_id = ?worker_id,\n                    \"mend: removed zero-activity agent log\"\n                );\n                summary.zero_activity_logs_cleaned += 1;\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendZeroActivityLogCleaned {\n                    worker_id: worker_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".to_string()),\n                    log_path: path.display().to_string(),\n                });\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check file age for retention-based cleanup.\n            let age = match file_age(path) {\n                Some(a) => a,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            if age <= cutoff {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"mend: failed to remove stale agent log\"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                path = %path.display(),\n                age_secs = age.as_secs(),\n                \"mend: removed stale agent log\"\n            );\n            summary.agent_logs_cleaned += 1;\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 4.5: Trace retention cleanup ───────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Clean up old traces based on retention policy.\n    ///\n    /// - Failed beads (non-zero exit): delete after trace_retention_failed_days\n    /// - Successful beads (exit 0): prune data after trace_retention_success_days, keep metadata only\n    fn cleanup_old_traces(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        if !self.traces_dir.exists() {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        match cleanup_traces(\n            &self.traces_dir,\n            self.trace_retention_failed_days,\n            self.trace_retention_success_days,\n        ) {\n            Ok(cleanup_summary) => {\n                summary.traces_pruned = cleanup_summary.traces_pruned;\n                summary.traces_cleaned = cleanup_summary.traces_deleted;\n\n                if cleanup_summary.traces_pruned > 0 || cleanup_summary.traces_deleted > 0 {\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendTraceCleanup {\n                        traces_pruned: cleanup_summary.traces_pruned,\n                        traces_deleted: cleanup_summary.traces_deleted,\n                    });\n\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        traces_pruned = cleanup_summary.traces_pruned,\n                        traces_deleted = cleanup_summary.traces_deleted,\n                        \"mend: cleaned up old traces\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: trace cleanup failed\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 4.75: Learning consolidation ───────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Clean up and consolidate workspace learnings.\n    ///\n    /// 1. Prune stale entries (>90 days without reinforcement)\n    /// 2. Consolidate if entries exceed max_learnings\n    fn cleanup_learnings(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut learnings = match LearningsFile::load(&self.workspace) {\n            Ok(l) => l,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::debug!(error = %e, \"mend: no learnings file to clean up\");\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        let _original_count = learnings.entries().len();\n\n        // Step 1: Prune stale entries\n        match learnings.prune_stale() {\n            Ok(pruned) => {\n                if pruned > 0 {\n                    tracing::info!(pruned, \"mend: pruned stale learning entries\");\n                    summary.learnings_pruned = pruned as u32;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: failed to prune stale learnings\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Consolidate if over limit\n        if learnings.entries().len() > self.max_learnings {\n            match learnings.consolidate(self.max_learnings) {\n                Ok(removed) => {\n                    if removed > 0 {\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            removed,\n                            max_count = self.max_learnings,\n                            \"mend: consolidated learning entries\"\n                        );\n                        summary.learnings_consolidated = removed as u32;\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: failed to consolidate learnings\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if summary.learnings_pruned > 0 || summary.learnings_consolidated > 0 {\n            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendLearningCleanup {\n                pruned: summary.learnings_pruned,\n                consolidated: summary.learnings_consolidated,\n            });\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 5: Database health check with auto-recovery ────────────────────\n\n    // ── Step 4.8: Idle worker flagging ─────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Flag workers that have been registered longer than `idle_timeout` with\n    /// zero beads processed. This helps identify workers that may have failed\n    /// to start, are stuck in dispatch, or have agent adapter problems.\n    ///\n    /// This is a warning/telemetry-only operation — idle workers are NOT\n    /// deregistered (they may be genuinely waiting for work).\n    fn flag_idle_workers(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        let workers = self.registry.list()?;\n\n        for worker in workers {\n            // Skip workers that have processed at least one bead.\n            if worker.beads_processed > 0 {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Calculate worker age from started_at.\n            let age = match Utc::now().signed_duration_since(worker.started_at).to_std() {\n                Ok(d) => d,\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %worker.id,\n                        \"worker started_at is in the future, skipping idle check\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            let idle_timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.config.idle_timeout);\n\n            if age > idle_timeout {\n                let age_secs = age.as_secs();\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id = %worker.id,\n                    pid = worker.pid,\n                    age_secs,\n                    idle_timeout_secs = self.config.idle_timeout,\n                    \"flagging idle worker (0 beads processed for longer than idle_timeout)\"\n                );\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendIdleWorkerFlagged {\n                    worker_id: worker.id.clone(),\n                    pid: worker.pid,\n                    age_secs,\n                });\n\n                summary.idle_workers_flagged += 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ── Step 4.9: Rate limiter state cleanup ─────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Clean up rate limiter state files.\n    ///\n    /// - Remove token bucket files for providers no longer in config\n    /// - Reset token buckets with stale last_refill (> 1 hour old) to full capacity\n    fn cleanup_rate_limit_state(&self, summary: &mut MendSummary) -> Result<()> {\n        use crate::rate_limit::TokenBucket;\n\n        let rate_limits_dir = self.state_dir.join(\"rate_limits\");\n\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&rate_limits_dir) {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    dir = %rate_limits_dir.display(),\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"mend: failed to read rate_limits directory for cleanup\"\n                );\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = match entry {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let path = entry.path();\n            let name = match path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) {\n                Some(n) => n,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Only consider JSON files (token bucket files).\n            if !name.ends_with(\".json\") {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Extract provider name from filename (e.g., \"anthropic.json\" -> \"anthropic\").\n            let provider = match name.strip_suffix(\".json\") {\n                Some(p) => p,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Check if provider exists in config.\n            let provider_in_config = self.limits_config.providers.contains_key(provider);\n\n            if !provider_in_config {\n                // Provider no longer in config — remove the file.\n                let age_secs = match file_age(&path) {\n                    Some(age) => age.as_secs(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n\n                match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {\n                    Ok(()) => {\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            provider,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            age_secs,\n                            \"removed rate limit state file for provider not in config\"\n                        );\n\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendRateLimitCleaned {\n                            provider: provider.to_string(),\n                            age_secs,\n                        });\n\n                        summary.rate_limit_providers_removed += 1;\n                        summary.rate_limits_cleaned += 1;\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            provider,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove rate limit state file\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Provider is in config — check if last_refill is stale (> 1 hour old).\n            let content = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n                Ok(c) => c,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::debug!(\n                        provider,\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to read rate limit state file\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            let mut bucket: TokenBucket = match serde_json::from_str(&content) {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::debug!(\n                        provider,\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to parse rate limit state file\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            let last_refill_age = match Utc::now()\n                .signed_duration_since(bucket.last_refill)\n                .to_std()\n            {\n                Ok(d) => d,\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::debug!(provider, \"last_refill is in the future, skipping reset\");\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            const STALE_THRESHOLD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3600); // 1 hour\n\n            if last_refill_age > STALE_THRESHOLD {\n                // Stale token bucket — reset to full capacity.\n                let age_secs = last_refill_age.as_secs();\n                bucket.tokens = bucket.capacity as f64;\n                bucket.last_refill = Utc::now();\n\n                match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&bucket) {\n                    Ok(json) => {\n                        if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(&path, &json) {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                provider,\n                                path = %path.display(),\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to write reset rate limit state file\"\n                            );\n                            continue;\n                        }\n\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            provider,\n                            age_secs,\n                            capacity = bucket.capacity,\n                            \"reset stale rate limit state to full capacity\"\n                        );\n\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendRateLimitProviderReset {\n                            provider: provider.to_string(),\n                            age_secs,\n                        });\n\n                        summary.rate_limit_providers_reset += 1;\n                        summary.rate_limits_cleaned += 1;\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            provider,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to serialize reset rate limit state\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Run `br doctor` to check database health. If issues are found,\n    /// escalate through the recovery pipeline:\n    ///\n    /// 1. `br doctor` (check only) → if warnings found:\n    /// 2. `br doctor --repair` → if fails:\n    /// 3. Full rebuild (rm .beads/beads.db + br sync --import + verify)\n    ///\n    /// If the full rebuild also fails, the JSONL itself may be corrupt.\n    async fn check_db_health(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        summary: &mut MendSummary,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        // Step 1: Probe with `br doctor` (no repair).\n        let check_result = store.doctor_check().await;\n\n        let needs_repair = match check_result {\n            Ok(report) => {\n                // Doctor succeeded. If there are warnings, escalate to repair.\n                !report.warnings.is_empty()\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                let msg = format!(\"{e:#}\");\n                if store.is_corruption_error(&msg) {\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"bead backend doctor detected corruption\");\n                    true\n                } else {\n                    // Non-corruption error (e.g., br not found). Propagate.\n                    return Err(e);\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        if !needs_repair {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Try `br doctor --repair`.\n        tracing::info!(\"database health check found issues, attempting repair\");\n        match store.doctor_repair().await {\n            Ok(report) => {\n                let warnings = report.warnings.len() as u32;\n                let fixed = report.fixed.len() as u32;\n                tracing::info!(warnings, fixed, \"br doctor --repair completed\");\n\n                let _ = self\n                    .telemetry\n                    .emit(EventKind::MendDbRepaired { warnings, fixed });\n\n                // Only mark as repaired if actual fixes were applied.\n                // If warnings persist without fixes, returning WorkCreated would\n                // cause an infinite restart loop without making progress.\n                if fixed > 0 {\n                    summary.db_repaired = true;\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n\n                // If doctor_repair succeeded but warnings persist without fixes,\n                // escalate to full rebuild. This prevents repeated Mend cycles\n                // where each evaluation calls doctor_repair which returns the\n                // same unfixed warnings without making progress.\n                if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        warnings,\n                        \"doctor --repair succeeded but warnings persist without fixes, escalating to full rebuild\"\n                    );\n                } else {\n                    // No warnings and no fixes - DB is clean, no work needed.\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"br doctor --repair failed, attempting full rebuild\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Full rebuild — rm db + br sync --import + verify.\n        match store.full_rebuild().await {\n            Ok(()) => {\n                tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL\");\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendDbRebuilt);\n\n                summary.db_rebuilt = true;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"full database rebuild failed — JSONL may be corrupt\"\n                );\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for MendStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"mend\"\n    }\n\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"strand.mend\",\n        skip(self, store),\n        fields(\n            needle.strand.name = \"mend\",\n            needle.strand.result = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.strand.duration_ms = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    async fn evaluate(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>) -> StrandResult {\n        let start = std::time::Instant::now();\n        let mut summary = MendSummary::default();\n\n        // Check if the home bead store exists. If not, skip this strand.\n        // This distinguishes between \"no home store configured\" (expected for\n        // roam-only workers) and \"home store is broken\" (unexpected error).\n        if !store.has_valid_store() {\n            tracing::info!(\n                \"Home workspace has no .beads/ directory — skipping Mend strand \\\n                 (expected for roam-only workers)\"\n            );\n            return StrandResult::Skipped {\n                reason: \"no_home_store\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n\n        // Step 1: Stale claim cleanup via peer monitoring.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_stale_claims(store, &mut summary).await {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: stale claim cleanup failed\");\n            return StrandResult::Error(StrandError::StoreError(e));\n        }\n\n        // Step 1.5: Agent log file cleanup.\n        // Must run BEFORE orphaned in-progress cleanup so that logs for in-progress\n        // beads are preserved (they're still InProgress when we check).\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_old_agent_logs(store, &mut summary).await {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: agent log cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Orphaned in-progress bead recovery (registry-based).\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(store, &mut summary).await {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: orphaned in-progress cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 2.3: Stale assignee cleanup on open beads.\n        if let Err(e) = self\n            .cleanup_stale_assignees_on_open_beads(store, &mut summary)\n            .await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: stale assignee cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 2.5: Orphaned heartbeat file removal.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_orphaned_heartbeats(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: orphaned heartbeat cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Orphaned lock file removal.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_orphaned_locks(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: orphaned lock cleanup failed\");\n            return StrandResult::Error(StrandError::StoreError(e));\n        }\n\n        // Step 4: Dependency link repair.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_stale_dependencies(store, &mut summary).await {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: dependency cleanup failed\");\n            return StrandResult::Error(StrandError::StoreError(e));\n        }\n\n        // Step 4.5: Dead worker registry cleanup.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_dead_workers(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: dead worker cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 5: Trace retention cleanup.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_old_traces(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: trace cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 5.5: Learning consolidation.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_learnings(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: learning cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 5.75: Idle worker flagging.\n        if let Err(e) = self.flag_idle_workers(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: idle worker flagging failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 5.875: Rate limiter state cleanup.\n        if let Err(e) = self.cleanup_rate_limit_state(&mut summary) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: rate limit state cleanup failed\");\n            // Non-fatal — continue with remaining steps.\n        }\n\n        // Step 6: Database health check.\n        if let Err(e) = self.check_db_health(store, &mut summary).await {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"mend: database health check failed\");\n            // DB check failure is non-fatal — continue with the summary.\n        }\n\n        // Emit cycle summary telemetry.\n        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MendCycleSummary {\n            beads_released: summary.beads_released,\n            locks_removed: summary.locks_removed,\n            deps_cleaned: summary.deps_cleaned,\n            db_repaired: summary.db_repaired,\n            db_rebuilt: summary.db_rebuilt,\n            agent_logs_cleaned: summary.agent_logs_cleaned,\n            zero_activity_logs_cleaned: summary.zero_activity_logs_cleaned,\n            traces_pruned: summary.traces_pruned,\n            traces_deleted: summary.traces_cleaned,\n            workers_deregistered: summary.workers_deregistered,\n            idle_workers_flagged: summary.idle_workers_flagged,\n            rate_limits_cleaned: summary.rate_limits_cleaned,\n            assignees_cleared: summary.assignees_cleared,\n        });\n\n        let result = if summary.did_work() {\n            tracing::info!(\n                beads_released = summary.beads_released,\n                locks_removed = summary.locks_removed,\n                deps_cleaned = summary.deps_cleaned,\n                db_repaired = summary.db_repaired,\n                db_rebuilt = summary.db_rebuilt,\n                agent_logs_cleaned = summary.agent_logs_cleaned,\n                traces_pruned = summary.traces_pruned,\n                traces_deleted = summary.traces_cleaned,\n                \"mend performed cleanup — restarting waterfall\"\n            );\n            StrandResult::WorkCreated\n        } else {\n            tracing::debug!(\"mend found nothing to clean\");\n            StrandResult::NoWork\n        };\n\n        // Record result and duration on the span\n        let duration_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.strand.result\", format!(\"{:?}\", result));\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.strand.duration_ms\", duration_ms);\n\n        result\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Get the age of a file based on its modification time.\nfn file_age(path: &Path) -> Option<Duration> {\n    let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path).ok()?;\n    let modified = metadata.modified().ok()?;\n    SystemTime::now().duration_since(modified).ok()\n}\n\n/// Try to acquire an exclusive flock on a file (non-blocking).\n///\n/// Returns `Ok(Some(file))` if acquired, `Ok(None)` if held by another process.\nfn try_acquire_flock(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<std::fs::File>> {\n    use fs2::FileExt;\n\n    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .read(true)\n        .write(true)\n        .open(path)?;\n\n    match file.try_lock_exclusive() {\n        Ok(()) => Ok(Some(file)),\n        Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => Ok(None),\n        Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Peer monitoring — stale claim release and crash cleanup.\n//!\n//! Detects crashed or stuck workers by reading heartbeat files and comparing\n//! them against the configured TTL. For crashed workers (stale heartbeat +\n//! dead PID), releases the claimed bead, removes the heartbeat file, and\n//! deregisters from the worker registry.\n//!\n//! This module is designed to be called by the Mend strand (Strand 2). No\n//! other strand should perform peer monitoring.\n//!\n//! Depends on: `bead_store`, `health`, `registry`, `telemetry`, `types`.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse chrono::Utc;\n\nuse crate::bead_store::BeadStore;\nuse crate::health::{HealthMonitor, StalePeer};\nuse crate::registry::Registry;\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// PeerCheckResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Summary of a peer monitoring check cycle.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct PeerCheckResult {\n    /// Number of crashed workers detected (dead PID).\n    pub crashed_count: u32,\n    /// Number of stuck workers detected (alive PID, stale heartbeat).\n    pub stuck_count: u32,\n    /// Number of beads released from crashed workers.\n    pub beads_released: u32,\n}\n\nimpl PeerCheckResult {\n    /// Whether any cleanup work was performed.\n    pub fn did_work(&self) -> bool {\n        self.beads_released > 0\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// PeerMonitor\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Monitors peer workers for crashes and stale heartbeats.\n///\n/// Constructed with references to shared infrastructure (bead store, registry,\n/// telemetry). Call `check_peers()` to run one monitoring cycle.\npub struct PeerMonitor<'a> {\n    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,\n    heartbeat_ttl: Duration,\n    own_worker_id: String,\n    store: &'a dyn BeadStore,\n    registry: &'a Registry,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> PeerMonitor<'a> {\n    /// Create a new peer monitor.\n    ///\n    /// - `heartbeat_dir`: path to `~/.needle/state/heartbeats/`\n    /// - `heartbeat_ttl`: how long before a heartbeat is considered stale\n    /// - `own_worker_id`: this worker's ID (excluded from peer checks)\n    /// - `store`: bead store for releasing orphaned beads\n    /// - `registry`: worker registry for deregistering crashed workers\n    /// - `telemetry`: telemetry emitter for peer events\n    pub fn new(\n        heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,\n        heartbeat_ttl: Duration,\n        own_worker_id: String,\n        store: &'a dyn BeadStore,\n        registry: &'a Registry,\n        telemetry: Telemetry,\n    ) -> Self {\n        PeerMonitor {\n            heartbeat_dir,\n            heartbeat_ttl,\n            own_worker_id,\n            store,\n            registry,\n            telemetry,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Run one peer monitoring cycle.\n    ///\n    /// Algorithm:\n    /// 1. Read all heartbeat files\n    /// 2. For each stale peer (excluding ourselves):\n    ///    a. If PID is dead → CRASHED: release bead, remove heartbeat, deregister\n    ///    b. If PID is alive → STUCK: emit warning only, do NOT release\n    /// 3. Return summary of actions taken\n    pub async fn check_peers(&self) -> Result<PeerCheckResult> {\n        let heartbeats = HealthMonitor::read_all_heartbeats(&self.heartbeat_dir)?;\n\n        let mut result = PeerCheckResult {\n            crashed_count: 0,\n            stuck_count: 0,\n            beads_released: 0,\n        };\n\n        for hb in &heartbeats {\n            // Skip our own heartbeat (match by qualified identity).\n            if hb.qualified_id == self.own_worker_id {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Only check stale heartbeats.\n            if !HealthMonitor::is_stale(hb, self.heartbeat_ttl) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            let pid_alive = HealthMonitor::check_pid_alive(hb.pid);\n            let stale_peer = StalePeer {\n                worker_id: hb.worker_id.clone(),\n                qualified_id: Some(hb.qualified_id.clone()),\n                pid: hb.pid,\n                pid_alive,\n                current_bead: hb.current_bead.clone(),\n                last_heartbeat: hb.last_heartbeat,\n                heartbeat_file: hb.heartbeat_file.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n                    self.heartbeat_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", hb.qualified_id))\n                }),\n            };\n\n            if pid_alive {\n                // STUCK: alive PID, stale heartbeat. Warn only — do NOT release.\n                self.handle_stuck_peer(&stale_peer)?;\n                result.stuck_count += 1;\n            } else {\n                // CRASHED: dead PID. Clean up.\n                let released = self.handle_crashed_peer(&stale_peer).await?;\n                result.crashed_count += 1;\n                if released {\n                    result.beads_released += 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if result.crashed_count > 0 || result.stuck_count > 0 {\n            tracing::info!(\n                crashed = result.crashed_count,\n                stuck = result.stuck_count,\n                beads_released = result.beads_released,\n                \"peer monitoring cycle complete\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(result)\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a stuck peer: alive PID but stale heartbeat.\n    ///\n    /// Safety: never release the bead, never kill the process. Alert only.\n    fn handle_stuck_peer(&self, peer: &StalePeer) -> Result<()> {\n        let age_secs = Utc::now()\n            .signed_duration_since(peer.last_heartbeat)\n            .num_seconds()\n            .max(0) as u64;\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            worker = %peer.worker_id,\n            pid = peer.pid,\n            age_secs,\n            bead = ?peer.current_bead,\n            \"peer is stuck (alive PID, stale heartbeat) — not releasing\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit peer.stale telemetry for each stuck peer.\n        if let Some(ref bead_id) = peer.current_bead {\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::StuckDetected {\n                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                age_secs,\n            })?;\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a crashed peer: dead PID, stale heartbeat.\n    ///\n    /// 1. Release the claimed bead (if any)\n    /// 2. Remove the heartbeat file\n    /// 3. Deregister from the worker registry\n    /// 4. Emit peer.crashed telemetry\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` if a bead was released.\n    async fn handle_crashed_peer(&self, peer: &StalePeer) -> Result<bool> {\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker = %peer.worker_id,\n            pid = peer.pid,\n            bead = ?peer.current_bead,\n            \"peer crashed — cleaning up\"\n        );\n\n        let mut bead_released = false;\n\n        // 1. Release the claimed bead (if any).\n        if let Some(ref bead_id) = peer.current_bead {\n            match self.store.release(bead_id).await {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        bead = %bead_id,\n                        worker = %peer.worker_id,\n                        \"released orphaned bead from crashed worker\"\n                    );\n                    bead_released = true;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    // Release failure is non-fatal — the bead may have already\n                    // been released or closed by another path.\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead = %bead_id,\n                        worker = %peer.worker_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to release bead from crashed worker (may already be released)\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Emit peer.crashed telemetry.\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::StuckReleased {\n                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                peer_worker: peer\n                    .qualified_id\n                    .as_deref()\n                    .unwrap_or(&peer.worker_id)\n                    .to_string(),\n            })?;\n        }\n\n        // 2. Remove the heartbeat file.\n        remove_heartbeat_file(&peer.heartbeat_file)?;\n\n        // 3. Deregister from the worker registry.\n        let dereg_id = peer.qualified_id.as_deref().unwrap_or(&peer.worker_id);\n        if let Err(e) = self.registry.deregister(dereg_id) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                worker = %peer.worker_id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to deregister crashed worker from registry\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(bead_released)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Remove a heartbeat file (best-effort).\nfn remove_heartbeat_file(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    match std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n        Ok(()) => {\n            tracing::debug!(path = %path.display(), \"removed stale heartbeat file\");\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n            // Already gone — not an error.\n            tracing::debug!(path = %path.display(), \"heartbeat file already removed\");\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            Err(e).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove heartbeat file: {}\", path.display()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n//    /// Convenience: claim a single bead by ID (fetches the bead, then delegates\n    /// to `claim_next` with a single-element candidate list).\n    ///\n    /// The `exclusions` parameter allows the caller to pass beads that should\n    /// be skipped (e.g., beads that recently lost a claim race). This prevents\n    /// tight loops when multiple workers are racing on the same bead.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is optional; if not provided, defaults to \"unknown\".\n    pub async fn claim_one(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        actor: &str,\n        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n        strand: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        let bead = self.store.show(bead_id).await?;\n\n        // If the bead is in the exclusion set, return NotClaimable immediately\n        // without attempting the claim. This prevents tight loops when the worker\n        // has already lost a race on this bead.\n        if exclusions.contains(bead_id) {\n            return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"bead is excluded\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        match self\n            .claim_next(&[bead], actor, exclusions, strand.unwrap_or(\"unknown\"))\n            .await?\n        {\n            ClaimOutcome::Claimed(b) => Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(b)),\n            ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost => Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost {\n                claimed_by: \"(race)\".to_string(),\n            }),\n            ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no candidates\".to_string(),\n            }),\n            ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e) => Err(e),\n            ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                bead_id,\n                consecutive_errors,\n                last_error,\n            } => Ok(ClaimResult::Suspect {\n                bead_id,\n                consecutive_errors,\n                last_error,\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify that a bead is still assigned to the expected worker at dispatch time.\n    ///\n    /// This prevents double-dispatch by checking the live bead store immediately\n    /// before agent execution. If another worker has reassigned the bead or the\n    /// bead has been released, the dispatch should be aborted.\n    ///\n    /// Returns:\n    /// - `Ok(true)`: bead is still in_progress and assigned to expected actor\n    /// - `Ok(false)`: bead is not assigned to expected actor (dispatch should abort)\n    /// - `Err(e)`: store error\n    pub async fn verify_claim_at_dispatch(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        expected_actor: &str,\n    ) -> Result<bool> {\n        match self.store.show(bead_id).await {\n            Ok(bead) => {\n                let is_valid = bead.status == BeadStatus::InProgress\n                    && bead.assignee.as_deref() == Some(expected_actor);\n                if !is_valid {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n                        expected_actor = %expected_actor,\n                        actual_status = ?bead.status,\n                        actual_assignee = ?bead.assignee,\n                        \"dispatch-time claim verification failed\"\n                    );\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimVerifyFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        expected_actor: expected_actor.to_string(),\n                        actual_status: format!(\"{:?}\", bead.status),\n                        actual_assignee: bead\n                            .assignee\n                            .clone()\n                            .unwrap_or_else(|| \"(none)\".to_string()),\n                    })?;\n                }\n                Ok(is_valid)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"dispatch-time claim verification encountered store error\"\n                );\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Atomically claim the next available bead using server-side selection.\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios. It calls\n    /// `BeadStore::claim_auto()` which atomically finds and claims a bead in\n    /// a single transaction, guaranteeing that concurrent workers receive\n    /// distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is the name of the strand that initiated the claim\n    /// (e.g., \"pluck\", \"mend\"). This is emitted in telemetry for the\n    /// `needle.beads.claimed` metric's `strand` attribute.\n    ///\n    /// Returns:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)`: successfully claimed a bead\n    /// - `NotClaimable(reason)`: no beads available to claim\n    /// - `StoreError(e)`: bead store error\n    pub async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str, strand: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimAttempt {\n            bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n            attempt: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        match self.store.claim_auto(actor).await {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead)) => {\n                let claim_event_count = match self.store.show_with_claim_history(&bead.id).await {\n                    Ok((_, count)) => count,\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            %error,\n                            \"unable to inspect claim history after atomic claim\"\n                        );\n                        None\n                    }\n                };\n                let in_memory_count = if claim_event_count.is_none() {\n                    Some(self.check_event_limit(&bead.id).unwrap_or(0))\n                } else {\n                    None\n                };\n                let event_count = claim_event_count.or(in_memory_count).unwrap_or(0);\n                if event_count >= MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD {\n                    let reason = self.trip_event_limit(&bead.id, event_count).await?;\n                    return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason });\n                }\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.bead.id\", bead.id.as_ref());\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"succeeded\");\n                self.telemetry.set_workspace(bead.workspace.clone());\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    priority: bead.priority as i32,\n                    strand: strand.to_string(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n            }\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason }) => {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason })\n            }\n            Ok(other) => {\n                // RaceLost shouldn't happen with claim_auto, but handle it\n                tracing::warn!(?other, \"claim_auto returned unexpected result\");\n                Ok(other)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic lock file path for a workspace.\n///\n/// Uses a simple hash (not crypto) of the workspace path. All workers\n/// compute the same hash for the same workspace.\nfn workspace_lock_path(lock_dir: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\n    workspace.hash(&mut hasher);\n    let hash = hasher.finish();\n    lock_dir.join(format!(\"needle-claim-{:016x}.lock\", hash))\n}\n\n/// Acquire an exclusive flock with a 10-second timeout.\n///\n/// Returns the locked file on success. The lock is released when the\n/// file is dropped (flock auto-releases on close).\npub async fn acquire_flock(lock_path: &Path) -> Result<std::fs::File> {\n    if let Some(parent) = lock_path.parent() {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n    }\n\n    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .truncate(false)\n        .write(true)\n        .open(lock_path)?;\n\n    let deadline = Instant::now() + FLOCK_TIMEOUT;\n    loop {\n        match file.try_lock_exclusive() {\n            Ok(()) => return Ok(file),\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                if Instant::now() >= deadline {\n                    return Err(anyhow!(\n                        \"flock timeout after {}s on {}\",\n                        FLOCK_TIMEOUT.as_secs(),\n                        lock_path.display()\n                    ));\n                }\n                tokio::time::sleep(FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests ��─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n267\t\n268\t/// How to extract token usage from agent output.\n269\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\n270\t#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n271\tpub enum TokenExtraction {\n272\t    /// Extract from JSON fields in stdout (e.g., Claude Code /// 1-based capture group index for output tokens.\n286\t        output_group: usize,\n287\t    },\n288\t    /// No token extraction.\n289\t    #[default]\n290\t    None,\n291\t}\n292\t\n293\t/// Extracted token usage from agent output.\n294\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n295\tpub struct TokenUsage {\n296\t    /// Input tokens consumed (None if extraction failed or not configured).\n297\t    pub input_tokens: Option<u64>,\n298\t    /// Output tokens produced (None if extraction failed or not configured).\n299\t    pub output_tokens: Option<u64>,\n300\t}\n301\t\n302\t/// Extract token usage from agent output using the configured method.\n303\tpub fn extract_tokens(extraction: &TokenExtraction, stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> TokenUsage {\n304\t    match extraction {\n305\t        TokenExtraction::None => TokenUsage::default(),\n306\t        TokenExtraction::JsonField {\n307\t            input_path,\n308\t            output_path,\n309\t        } => extract_tokens_json(stdout, input_path, output_path),\n310\t        TokenExtraction::Regex {\n311\t            pattern,\n312\t            input_group,\n313\t            output_group,\n314\t        } => {\n315\t            // *output_group)\n318\t        }\n319\t    }\n320\t}\n321\t\n322\t/// Extract tokens from JSON output using dot-separated path notation.\n323\tfn extract_tokens_json(stdout: &str, input_path: &str, output_path: &str) -> TokenUsage {\n324\t    let parsed: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(stdout) {\n325\t        Ok(v) => v,\n326\t        Err(_) => return TokenUsage::default(),\n327\t    };\n328\t\n329\t    let input_tokens = resolve_json_path(&parsed, input_path).and_then(|v| v.as_u64());\n330\t    let output_tokens = resolve_json_path(&parsed, output_path).and_then(|v| v.as_u64());\n331\t\n332\t    TokenUsage {\n333\t        input_tokens,\n334\t        output_tokens,\n335\t    }\n336\t}\n337\t\n338\t/// Resolve a dot-separated path in a JSON value (e.g., `result.usage.input_tokens`).\n339\tfn resolve_json_path<'a>(\n340\t    value: &'a serde_json::Value,\n341\t    path: &str,\n342\t) -> Option<&'a serde_json::Value> {\n343\t    let mut current = value;\n344\t    for key in path.split('.') {\n345\t        current = current.get(key)?;\n346\t    }\n347\t    Some(current)\n348\t}\n349\t\n350\t/// Extract tokens from text using a regex with numbered capture groups.\n351\tfn extract_tokens_regex(\n352\t    text: &str,\n353\t    pattern: &str,\n354\t    input_group: usize,\n355\t    output_group: usize,\n356\t) -> TokenUsage {\n357\t    let re = match Regex::new(pattern) {\n358\t        Ok(r) => r,\n359\t        Err(_) => return TokenUsage::default(),\n360\t    };\n361\t\n362\t    let caps = match re.captures(text) {\n363\t        Some(c) => c,\n364\t        None => return TokenUsage::default(),\n365\t    };\n366\t\n367\t    let parse_group = |group: usize| -> Option<u64> {\n368\t        caps.get(group)?\n369\t            .as_str()\n370\t            .replace(',', \"\")\n371\t            .parse::<u64>()\n372\t            .ok()\n373\t    };\n374\t\n375\t    TokenUsage {\n376\t        input_tokens: parse_group(input_group),\n377\t        output_tokens: parse_group(output_group),\n378\t    }\n379\t}\n380\t\n381\t//
